question: Which document, slice, schema, format, diagnostic and application contracts should own external document imports, and which editing-runtime requirements can disappear?
trigger: User requests harsh honest feedback on the completed conversion-correctness-guarantees report, including corrected prior diagnoses, loss impact API, registry consumer and gate claims.
requirements: Keep format-owned parsing, loss-aware clipboard negotiation, fitter-owned contextual placement and registry-owned notifications.
Report discarded user content even when no HTML node survives, fallback text survives, or security policy requires removal; quiet harmless metadata/event-attribute cleanup.
Retain proven fixes and explicitly correct the prior review's unsupported slice-loss and trailing-paragraph diagnoses.
Assess current implementation without product repairs, new architecture, publication, or reopening deferred Yjs/Markdown-streaming work.
evidenceReuse: Read the current plan and execution plus the prior import review. Inspected generated-editor contracts, report owner routing, HTML mapping and sanitizer, and registry callback. Re-ran four slice refusal/join tests and two DataTransfer/owner tests (all pass), ledger and Plate Next v246 checks (pass), and Plite typecheck:tests (six TS2322 failures). Ran six new package-DOM probes: five fail their loss-reporting assertions; the Docs metadata control passes. Earlier browser receipts retain their scope and were not rerun.
summary: Pursue three bounded HTML loss-reporting repairs; keep the accepted API and owner split. Unsupported-only HTML discards diagnosed loss by returning null for an empty successful slice, yielding lossy:false for plain fallback or total refusal. Embedded media with fallback children skips unsupported-content reporting and succeeds under default reject. Blanket html-unsafe-content => lossless hides removed SVG and object fallback content. Keep security removal, but classify actual impact at its source. Retain atomic fitter refusal, cross-block joining, runtime-owner routing and generated-editor narrowing. All-gates-pass is false: Plite test types still fail six times. No substrate redesign or video mapping is required to repair these reporting defects.

reconciliation.reason: The claim that insertion dropped content, and that cross-block joining created the kit's trailing paragraph, were misdiagnoses. The latest implementation explains silent negotiation fallback and TrailingBlockPlugin; four current slice tests pass. Do not restore strict grammar admission or suppress configured trailing-block policy.

reconciliation.question: Which document, slice, schema, format, diagnostic and application contracts should own external document imports, and which editing-runtime requirements can disappear?
reconciliation.reason: Retain corrected diagnoses, list target fix, runtime-owner routing and the narrower generated-editor type contract. Reopen only completeness of paste loss reporting: five executable assertions expose three uncovered paths. A fresh Plite typecheck:tests run also confirms the six recorded errors, so the tree is not wholly green.

alternatives: Keep explicit warning impact, the settled DataTransfer report and the registry callback; repair empty-result diagnostic preservation, unmapped media detection with surviving children, and sanitizer impact classification at their HTML owners. Pursue: removes three proven information-loss paths without adding a public noun, state owner, observer or runtime layer.

Delete the report/impact API or derive warnings from diagnostic codes in registry UI. Stop: a current user needs to know when paste loses content, and copied UI cannot reconstruct discarded diagnostics or safely infer format semantics.

Require full closed-element grammar at slice admission or redesign the fitter to repair these failures. Stop: existing refusal and joining guards pass; the defect is diagnostic loss during format decoding/negotiation, and contextual lossless fitting remains legitimate.

Treat all sanitizer removals as harmless to keep Google Docs quiet. Stop: the passing metadata/event-attribute control does not justify classifying deleted SVG graphics or object fallback text as lossless.
Add HTML video support, broaden to Firefox/WebKit, or redesign Yjs/streaming Markdown now. Defer outside this review: these are independent capabilities and do not prevent truthful loss reporting.
proofLimits: Source/HappyDOM proof only for new findings: six probes, one pass and five expected-correctness assertions failing. Four slice refusal/join tests and two DataTransfer/report-owner tests pass. Plite typecheck:tests fails with six TS2322 diagnostics in authored-fragment-provider.test.tsx; upstream attribution was supplied by the user and not independently bisected. Ledger and Plate Next v246 passed before review recording. No fresh browser, full package suite, benchmark, exported-artifact, Firefox or WebKit proof. The initial probe run contained an invalid editor.destroy cleanup; the corrected retained final run has only the five behavioral failures. Product source is unchanged. Existing browser toast evidence is a one-time receipt, not a newly run or durable toast regression.
